Name: Compilation with Insufficient Warnings or Errors
Description: The code is compiled without sufficient warnings enabled.

CommonConsequences.Note: This issue makes it more difficult to maintain the product, which indirectly affects security by making it more difficult or time-consuming to find and/or fix vulnerabilities. It also might make it easier to introduce vulnerabilities.
This issue may prevent the detection of subtle bugs or quality issues.

MappingNotes.Rationale: This CWE entry is at the Base level of abstraction, which is a preferred level of abstraction for mapping to the root causes of vulnerabilities.
MappingNotes.Comments: Carefully read both the name and description to ensure that this mapping is an appropriate fit. Do not try to 'force' a mapping to a lower-level Base/Variant simply to comply with this preferred level of abstraction.

DetectionMethods.Description: Inspect scripts and tools that invoke the compiler. Ensure that the appropriate command line switches and/or configuration are specified to report warnings and errors.

PotentialMitigations.Description: Compile the code with the best options available to generate the most warnings that are actionable.
PotentialMitigations.EffectivenessNotes: Compilers with maximum settings could generate too many warnings that are not directly actionable to the developer. The developer should also be careful to know that some options might not actually generate all possible warnings that the compiler can detect. For example, in C, the GCC compiler's "-Wall" option does not actually capture all possible warnings.

ContentHistory.SubmissionComment: Entry derived from Common Quality Enumeration (CQE) Draft 0.9.
